newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court injunction halts CRT shr transfer.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court injunction halts CRT shr transfer.

text.p: A Brazilian court injunction has halted the transfer of a 35-percent stake in state telecom CRT bought last week by a group including Spain's Telefonica de Espana, a state spokesman said.
"The state has filed an appeal to have the injunction lifted," the spokesman for Rio Grande do Sul state told Reuters. "We are completely confident that will happen, though it may take a few days."
He said the injunction, sought by the Workers' Party (PT), bars the transfer of CRT shares to the consortium that won December 17 bidding on the strategic stake in the company.
PT protested the sale on grounds the state does not really own the block of voting common shares because they were used as collateral for outstanding loans.

It was the latest of 18 lawsuits filed in recent months to block the sale of the strategic stake in CRT. Sixteen of the complaints were tossed out while one prompted in a last-minute change in bid specifications, delaying the auction for two hours.
On Christmas Eve, Chief Judge Joao Adalberto Medeiros Fernandes of the state's Justice Court granted the injunction on the basis of the PT party's complaint. But the state has brushed off the suit.

"There is no news here," the state's Energy, Mines and Communications Office said in a statement. "This argument was used as a basis for other legal actions and will be decided by the Justice Court in favor of the state."
The group that won bidding on the shares of CRT, formally called Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes, also included Brazil's RBS Participacoes, Telefonica de Argentina, CTC of Chile and Citicorp.

The consortium's offer of 681 million reais, some 54.8 percent above base price, beat a bid by a group that included Italy's Stet and stunned analysts. By law, the state must retain a 51-percent controlling stake in CRT.
The auction was closely watched by the market because it was the first opening of Brazil's massive telecommunications sector to private capital.
The Brazilian government next year expects to break up and begin selling off the federal Telebras as well as grant concessions for operating cellular concessions on the B Band frequency.
